The groups stay dense in every panel, while the plain edges between them grow from none to 3 to 9 and blur the split." width="100%"} Creates `num_groups` groups of `group_size` nodes and joins each pair of nodes at random: with probability `p_in` if they are in the same group and with probability `p_out` if they are not, every pair independently. When `p_in > p_out` the groups are communities, denser inside than between, and the closer the two probabilities, the harder they are to detect. This is the stochastic block model with equal groups and only two probabilities; for groups of different sizes see `add_random_partition_graph()`. Each node's group (`0`, `1`, ...) is stored in the `community_attr=` node attribute, so the planted communities can be compared with what a detection method finds. The groups are created in order, each as a consecutive run of node IDs. In an undirected graph each pair is joined at most once and edges point from the earlier-created node to the later one; in a directed graph each ordered pair is drawn separately, so two nodes may be joined in both directions. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Planted partition graphs are the standard model for: - benchmarking community detection, with a known answer and adjustable difficulty - studying detectability: below a sharp threshold in `p_in - p_out`, no method can recover the groups better than chance - generating networks with assortative (`p_in > p_out`) or disassortative (`p_in < p_out`) group structure ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [num_groups]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of groups. Must be at least `1`. [group_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in each group. Must be at least `1`. [p_in]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of an edge between two nodes in the same group, between `0` and `1`. [p_out]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Probability of an edge between two nodes in different groups, between `0` and `1`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [community_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's group. Default is `"community"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `num_groups=` or `group_size=` is less than `1`, or `p_in=` or `p_out=` is not between `0` and `1`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Four groups of 25 nodes, with edges ten times as likely inside a group as between groups: ::: {#1c310b29 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_planted_partition_graph( num_groups=4, group_size=25, p_in=0.3, p_out=0.03, seed=1 ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (100, 477) ``` ::: ::: The expected edge count is `4 * C(25, 2) * 0.3 + C(4, 2) * 25^2 * 0.03 = 360 + 112.5`, and about three quarters of the edges fall inside a group: ::: {#31401194 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} coverage, _ = graph.partition_quality("community") round(coverage, 2), round(graph.modularity("community"), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.77, 0.51) ``` ::: ::: Louvain, which never sees the planted groups, finds four groups that score as well as they do: ::: {#5cb353c2 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} found = graph.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) len(set(found.values())), round(graph.modularity(found), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (4, 0.51) ``` ::: :::
